# Song Leader Training

A cappella song-leading practice tool with real-time pitch detection, hymn melody playback, and a YIN-algorithm grading system. Client-side only React app, no backend, no auth.

## Tech Stack

| Layer | Tech |
|---|---|
| Frontend | React 18.3.1, Vite 6, Canvas API, Web Audio API + AudioWorklet, VexFlow 5 (notation), @tonejs/midi 2 (MIDI parsing) |
| Backend | None (client-side only) — no server runtime; `package.json` declares no `engines` field |
| Data | Static JSON in `public/` (`hymn_index.json`, `hymn_melodies/`); no database, no localStorage |
| Auth | None |
| Hosting | Vercel (`vercel.json` headers block) |
| Testing | None |
| Integrations | Google Fonts (DM Sans + DM Serif Display via CSS `@import`), `soundfont-player` fetching `church_organ` from `gleitz.github.io` (MusyngKite CDN), `getUserMedia` for microphone |

### Key Files
- `src/App.jsx` (1,430 lines) — entire UI, meter engine, melody generator, hymn loader, practice/grading flow, inline CSS (`const css = ...` at line 259).
- `src/audio/pitch-engine.js` (610 lines) — main-thread controller wrapping the AudioWorklet; smoothing pipeline (outlier rejection → median filter → EMA).
- `public/pitch-processor.js` (350 lines) — AudioWorklet running YIN with parabolic interpolation on a dedicated audio thread.
- `src/audio/grader.js` (404 lines) — pitch accuracy / rhythm / stability scoring.
- `src/audio/recorder.js` (380 lines) — AudioRecorder class capturing pitch history during practice.
- `src/components/NotationDisplay.jsx` (363 lines) — VexFlow renderer.
- `src/components/PitchVisualizer.jsx` (360 lines) — Canvas pitch display, bypasses React for 60fps.
- `vercel.json` — full security header block (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy).

### Data Flow
Mic → `getUserMedia` → `AudioContext` → `public/pitch-processor.js` AudioWorklet runs YIN per buffer → posts pitch frames to `pitch-engine.js` → smoothing pipeline → `PitchVisualizer.jsx` renders on Canvas (no React re-render). Hymn data: `public/hymn_index.json` fetched in `App.jsx:538` → on selection, `App.jsx:495` tries `/hymn_midi/<id>.mid` then falls back to `/hymn_melodies/<id>.json` (`App.jsx:513`) → `midi-parser.js` decodes → `NotationDisplay.jsx` renders the staff via VexFlow → `grader.js` compares detected pitches against reference frames. Every fetch target is a same-origin relative path built from a static hymn index — no user-controlled URLs anywhere.

### External API Calls
- `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=DM+Sans...&family=DM+Serif+Display` — GET via CSS `@import` in the inline stylesheet at `src/App.jsx:259`, fires on page load.
- `https://fonts.gstatic.com/...` — GET, font files pulled by the above `@import`.
- `https://gleitz.github.io/midi-js-soundfonts/MusyngKite/...` — GET via `Soundfont.instrument(..., 'church_organ')` at `src/App.jsx:475`, triggered when the user starts melody playback.
- `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/...` — GET, fallback soundfont host permitted by the CSP `connect-src` directive.

### Accepted Risks
- **No authentication** — intentional. Public hymn-singing practice tool with no user data and no accounts.
- **Public GitHub repo** — `taylorzeltwanger91/Song-Leader-Training` is public. No secrets in the codebase or in git history (AWS/OpenAI/GitHub/Slack token sweeps all clean this scan), so public visibility is safe.
- **`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on static assets** — verified served this scan. There are no API routes and no auth, so there is nothing cross-origin to protect.
- **`script-src 'unsafe-eval'` in CSP** — required by `soundfont-player` (uses the `Function` constructor) and `@tonejs/midi`. Acceptable for a static tool that accepts no user-supplied input.
- **Empty / graceful catch blocks in audio paths** — `src/App.jsx:290, 630, 635, 642, 659, 877, 1122` and the audio modules swallow errors to degrade gracefully around optional Web Audio APIs (feature-detection and cleanup pattern). No auth, payment, webhook, or data-write path is involved, so these are not `swallowed-exception`. One to keep an eye on: `src/App.jsx:541` (`.catch(() => setHymnIndex([]))`) turns a failed hymn-index fetch into a silently empty hymn list with no `console.error` — a debuggability gap rather than a security one.
- **Console statements in audio modules** — `recorder.js`, `pitch-engine.js`, `midi-parser.js`, `NotationDisplay.jsx` use `console.warn`/`console.error` for legitimate audio diagnostics. The lone `console.log` at `src/audio/midi-parser.js:175` logs MIDI parse metadata (title, track/note counts) — no sensitive data.

## Guardrails

### Universal (apply to all projects)

1. Never hardcode API keys or secrets — use `.env` + `.env.example` from first commit
2. Every API route needs CORS origin validation, input validation, and auth
3. Write RLS/Firestore rules the same day you create a table
4. Never use `innerHTML` with dynamic data — use `textContent` or framework escaping
5. API proxies must restrict destination URLs with an allowlist (SSRF prevention)
6. Auth cookies must contain signed claims (HMAC), not plain booleans
7. If a secret was ever committed to a public repo, rotate it immediately
8. No `console.log` with sensitive data in production
9. Run `npx prettier --write .` before committing — keep a `.prettierrc` in the repo root

### Project-Specific
- **Do not add code to `src/App.jsx`.** It is already 1,430 lines. New features go in new files under `src/components/` or `src/audio/`. When fixing a bug there, extract the surrounding section while you are in it.
- **Delete the legacy root `zions-hymns-trainer*.jsx` files** when touching related functionality — they are not imported by anything and only pollute search results.
- **Do not introduce auth, env vars, or backend services.** This is a local practice tool by design. If a feature needs server state, raise it before implementing.
- **Pin or self-host the soundfont before swapping CDNs.** `soundfont-player` is unmaintained; if it breaks, the migration path is a maintained alternative plus a bundled `church_organ` asset, not a fresh remote CDN.
- **Keep the CSP in `vercel.json` intact.** Any new external host (analytics, fonts, audio source) needs an explicit `connect-src`/`style-src`/`font-src` entry — do not weaken `default-src 'self'`.
- **Replace `innerHTML` with `textContent` in `src/components/NotationDisplay.jsx:306`.** The render-error fallback concatenates `e.message` into `innerHTML`; build a `<div>` and set `.textContent`. Low risk today, but a Guardrail #4 violation.
- **Run `npm audit fix` on the next touch.** The dev-tooling advisories do not ship, but the `vite` dev-server ones are live on a Windows dev box while `npm run dev` is running.

## Strengths

The full security-header set (CSP with a locked-down `default-src 'self'`, HSTS, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy) is verified live in production rather than merely configured; the app carries no secrets, env vars, or backend attack surface at all; every fetch target is a same-origin relative path built from a static index, so there is no user-controlled-URL sink anywhere; ESLint `no-undef` is enforced through a `prebuild` lint gate that cannot be skipped by a normal build; and YIN pitch detection is correctly isolated to an AudioWorklet thread.

## Scope & Boundaries
Local-only, client-side practice tool for a cappella song leaders. No accounts, no server state, no analytics, no payments. Hymn data is checked into `public/`. Microphone is requested at runtime for pitch detection; nothing leaves the device.

Out of scope: multi-user features, cloud sync, recordings being uploaded anywhere, AI grading, monetization.

## Conventions
- Single-file `App.jsx` is intentional — extract only when adding a new feature or when the file forces a search miss.
- Inline CSS as a `const css = ...` template literal injected once is the established pattern. Don't introduce a CSS framework.
- Audio modules use `console.warn`/`console.error` for diagnostics; `console.log` is reserved for one-off MIDI parse summaries (and even those should be cleaned up).
- React component files are PascalCase; audio modules are kebab-case.
- VexFlow and Canvas paths bypass React rendering on purpose for 60 fps; do not "fix" by lifting state.

## Key Patterns
- **YIN on AudioWorklet:** pitch detection runs on the audio thread (`public/pitch-processor.js`), main thread only handles smoothing and rendering. This is a hard performance ceiling — keep it.
- **Smoothing pipeline:** outlier rejection → median filter → EMA. Tweaks should be unit-tested with recorded fixtures, not eyeballed.
- **Grading:** `grader.js` consumes a reference melody (frames with start/end/midi) and a detected pitch trace, returns pitch / rhythm / stability scores 0-100.
- **Hymn loading:** lazy fetch on selection. `hymn_index.json` is the only file always loaded.

## Common Issues
- **`unsafe-eval` in CSP** is required by `soundfont-player` (uses `Function` constructor). Removing it breaks playback in all major browsers.
- **iOS Safari** requires a user gesture to resume `AudioContext`. The mic-start button is the gesture; do not auto-start.
- **MusyngKite CDN** occasionally 404s — `connect-src` already allows the GitHub-raw fallback so soundfont-player can fail over.
- **VexFlow 5** changed several factory APIs from VexFlow 4 — pin and read changelogs before bumping.

## Session Maintenance Protocol

At the end of every substantive session, propose targeted edits to CLAUDE.md or `.claude/rules/*.md`. Domain-specific detail belongs in the rule file, not here. The SCAN:AUTO block above is auto-managed — never hand-edit; the next scan will overwrite.
